inputs.share_count_basis: 56.474M Class A + Class B shares outstanding at 30 June 2026 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q balance sheet: 47.925M A + 8.549M B), plus ~0.25M Class A shares issued on 10 July 2026 for the Ellsworth acquisition ($24.8M of stock; share count ESTIMATED at ~$100/share because the 10-Q gives the dollar value only), plus ~0.3M for unvested PSU/RSU dilution (Q3 diluted less basic weighted average was 0.36M). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and acquisitions are not modelled so no acquisition stock is issued.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow-statement share-based compensation add-back, TTM to 30 June 2026 = FY2025 37.0 - 9M FY2025 28.0 + 9M FY2026 31.2 = 40.2 (ROAD_Annual_FY2025.txt:2571, ROAD_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt cash flow statement). The Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation shows a smaller SBC line (FY2025 28.8; 9M FY2026 21.8) because acquisition-related award expense is classified under transformative acquisition expenses; the cash-flow figure is the complete one. PLUS purchase of treasury stock, TTM 32.5 (FY2025 23.5 - 9M FY2025 20.8 + 9M FY2026 29.8), which the 10-Q describes as shares taken from employees to reimburse income taxes paid on vesting restricted stock, i.e. equity-award withholding tax, not an open-market buyback. The filer publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per house rule. This is the conservative reading: the withholding cash is arguably the mechanism that keeps the count flat rather than an additional cost.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year US Treasury), equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.2 for a levered regional contractor/materials producer -> cost of equity ~10.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt 5.9% (the company's own June 2026 weighted-average SOFR-based rate, Q3 FY2026 10-Q Item 3), ~4.4% after tax. Capital structure at market: ~72% equity / ~28% debt -> ~8.7%, rounded up to 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in every scenario: risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not through a WACC spread.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (US GAAP operating leases): operating lease cost sits inside cost of revenues, above Adjusted EBITDA, so the lease charge is already in the flows. Operating lease liabilities (105.4 at 30 June 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt and lease_cost_pct_path is zero. No finance-lease balance is disclosed separately.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. No noncontrolling interest; the one joint venture is immaterial (equity-method loss of 0.001 in 9M FY2026).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, three scenarios, 10-year horizon. Routed as a US operating company (vertically integrated hot-mix asphalt, aggregates and paving contractor across eight Sunbelt states); not a bank, REIT or holdco. No memory entry and no prior DCF: this is a fresh build. No ROAD_Analysis.json existed at build time, so narratives rest on the 10-K/10-Q text and the KPI table only. BASE PERIOD: FY2026 ended 30 September 2026 but the 10-K is not yet filed, so FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 June 2026 (FY2025 less 9M FY2025 plus 9M FY2026) and Year 1 is the twelve months to 30 June 2027. Replace with FY2026 actuals and FY2027 guidance when the 10-K lands. NET DEBT is pro forma: debt principal 1,803.25 at 30 June 2026 plus the 77.2 cash consideration for Ellsworth (closed 10 July 2026, funded from cash and the revolver) less cash 94.5; restricted cash and captive-insurer restricted investments are excluded. A further contingent earn-out of up to 10.0 on Ellsworth is not included. ACQUISITIONS ARE NOT MODELLED: the growth paths are organic plus the annualisation of deals already closed, and no acquisition cash or stock is spent. The company's stated strategy and its 2030 revenue target depend on continued deal-making; that is upside or downside the model leaves out on both sides (revenue and purchase price). last_fcf is the house formula on REPORTED free cash flow (operating cash flow 352.8 less gross capex 177.3), which is after ~107 of cash interest; the forward flows are unlevered, so last_fcf is not directly comparable to Year 1 FCF. ADJUSTED EBITDA as the company defines it adds back share-based compensation and transformative-acquisition expenses and includes gains on equipment sales (TTM ~15); SBC is deducted again in the build, capex is taken gross of disposal proceeds (TTM proceeds 30.9) as the offset. BUYBACKS: a $50M programme to September 2028 exists, but cash spent on treasury stock to date is award-tax withholding; the flat count is a modelling convention that the company funds only in part. The price is a regular close near the bottom of the 52-week range (74.51-151.0); the cause of the drawdown was not established from the filings on hand.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic revenue growth (company-disclosed: 8.7% FY2023, 6.8% FY2024, 8.4% FY2025, 8.9% Q3 FY2026), not the equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (17.9%) is more than 30% below the revenue CAGR (29.0%), and both are acquisition-driven: revenue because roughly three quarters of FY2025 growth was acquired, equity because stock was issued for Lone Star Paving and P&S. Neither is a usable organic growth anchor, so the disclosed organic growth rate is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Fiscal years to 30 September, FY2020/FY2022 to FY2025. Owner FCF = reported FCF - cash-flow SBC - treasury stock purchases (award-tax withholding): FY2020 51.0, FY2022 -60.4, FY2025 92.9. The 3-year owner-FCF CAGR is undefined because FY2022 was negative. Owner-FCF 5-year CAGR of 12.7% compares with 23.9% on reported FCF: SBC plus withholding rose from 1.6 to 60.5 over the period, so a growing share of reported cash flow growth is being paid for in stock. EPS 3-year CAGR is off a depressed FY2022 base (0.41).

base.growth_rates_note: Year 1 (twelve months to June 2027) = ~7% organic plus ~6 points from annualising deals already closed (P&S, Baytown, middle Tennessee and others in FY2026; Ellsworth in July 2026). Thereafter organic only, fading from the 7-9% the company has reported to 3%.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 15.1% in FY2025 and 15.0% TTM (522.5 on 3,477.9). Ramps to 16.5%, short of the company's ~17% 2030 aspiration.
base.sbc_pct_path_note: TTM SBC plus award-tax withholding was 2.09% of revenue, inflated by acquisition-related grants; path starts at 1.9% and declines to 1.4%.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: Cash taxes paid were 5.5 in FY2025 and 5.2 in 9M FY2026 against a book provision of 32.7 and 28.1: bonus depreciation and tax-deductible acquisition goodwill defer most of the bill. The rate on EBIT ramps from 12% to a normal 25% (21% federal plus state) over six years rather than perpetuating the shelter.
base.capex_pct_path_note: TTM gross capex 177.3 (5.1% of revenue); FY2026 guidance 165-185 including growth capex. Held at or slightly above D&A through the terminal year.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Negative: a contractor's receivables, retainage, unbilled work and inventory exceed payables and billings in excess, so growth consumes cash.

scenario_narratives.base: State DOT and municipal paving budgets across the eight Sunbelt states keep growing with population and lane-mile wear, and the record $3.4B backlog (2.7 uncompleted, 0.7 low-bid at June 2026) converts on schedule. Year 1 carries the annualisation of the FY2026 deals and Ellsworth; after that revenue grows organically at 7% fading to 3%, with no further acquisitions modelled. Vertical integration (109 HMA plants, 17 aggregates facilities, 3 liquid asphalt terminals at FY2025) and plant utilisation lift Adjusted EBITDA margin from 15.0% to 16.5%, a little short of management's ~17% goal. The tax deferral from bonus depreciation and deductible goodwill unwinds to a 25% cash rate by year six, and capex stays at or above depreciation.
scenario_narratives.bull: Organic growth runs at 8-9% for five years as Sunbelt migration, strong state funding and private commercial and residential site work compound, and the acquired platforms in Texas, Oklahoma and Tennessee are brought up to legacy-market margins. Liquid asphalt terminals and aggregates self-supply push Adjusted EBITDA margin to 17.5%, modestly above the 2030 target, while capital intensity eases as plants are filled rather than built. Even this case excludes future acquisitions, so it is a statement about the existing footprint only.
scenario_narratives.bear: Public funding stalls: federal surface-transportation money (the five-year IIJA authorisation ran to 30 September 2026) is extended late or flat, state lettings slow, and private site work weakens with higher rates. After the acquisition annualisation in year 1, organic revenue is flat for two years, bid margins compress as competitors chase a smaller pool of work, and liquid asphalt and diesel costs are not fully passed through on fixed-price contracts, taking Adjusted EBITDA margin to 13%, roughly where it was in FY2024 (12.1%) before the Lone Star mix uplift. With ~$1.8B of floating-rate debt against a thinner EBITDA base, leverage rises above 4x and acquisitions stop. The business survives on maintenance paving but re-rates as an ordinary contractor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%, above the 15% default: net debt is about 3.4x TTM Adjusted EBITDA, all of it floating-rate, and roughly two thirds of revenue depends on public budgets at a moment when the federal highway authorisation is up for renewal. Base 50%: organic growth of 7-9% and a 15% margin are what the company is reporting now, and backlog covers most of the next twelve months. Bull 30%, below the 35% default: it needs both sustained high-single-digit organic growth and a margin above management's own target.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Construction Partners is valued as the cash stream of its existing footprint: organic growth plus the deals already closed, margins built from components, SBC and award-tax withholding expensed, and the cash-tax shelter ramped away. Acquisitions, which have supplied most of the growth since FY2022 and consumed about $1.3B of cash in the last seven quarters, are deliberately left out on both sides. The market price therefore has to be read against a model that gives no credit for future deal-making; the gap between the two is the value the market assigns to the roll-up continuing at attractive prices.
key_risks_to_valuation: Acquisitions are excluded: if the company keeps buying at 8-10x EBITDA and integrating to legacy margins, value is understated; if it overpays or leverage bites, the omitted cash outflow matters more than the omitted revenue.
Leverage: ~$1.79B pro forma net debt, all floating at ~5.9%; each 1% rate move is $18M of annual interest (10-Q Item 3). Equity value per share moves about $1.75 for every $100M of enterprise value.
Federal and state highway funding: timing and size of the next surface-transportation authorisation after September 2026.
Cash tax: the model ramps to 25% by year six; continued bonus depreciation on a growing fleet could keep cash taxes lower for longer, which is upside to the base case.
Base period is a trailing twelve months to June 2026, not a reported fiscal year; FY2026 results and FY2027 guidance are not yet in the model.
SBC basis: summing the SBC add-back and award-tax withholding (2.1% of revenue TTM) is the conservative house treatment; on the add-back alone (1.2%) value would be a few dollars per share higher.
Adjusted EBITDA excludes transformative-acquisition expenses (14.2 in 9M FY2026) that recur for a serial acquirer.
